plot: The night before the movers come, Zeek's Plan Lunch is to ride to the new house in Mia's lunchbox, but his numbers say only four bros fit and someone must stay behind; while hiding from Dad's midnight snack run, scared Pim dives under the box and finds what Zeek's measuring from above missed — a hidden bottom drawer — so the bros carry Mia's forty crayons to her pencil case (rescuing her favorite blue one), all five fit on two floors, and at dawn Dad sets the lunchbox on the car roof and starts the engine.

beats.say: Zeek! My head is stuck in the lid! Help!
Hold still! You're ruining my packing diagram!
Wednesday night. The movers come tomorrow. The truck takes no food.
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Mia's lunchbox rides in the car. On her lap. Safe.
Zeek calls it Plan Lunch. He drew it on a napkin.
Love it. Everyone in. Biggest first. That's me.
Bup goes in. Lolly goes in. Her points stick out.
Ow. Ow. Who packed a grape in here?
Crispy rolls in. The cheese stick starts to sweat.
Sorry, cheese. I run warm.
Zeek squeezes in. Then there's Pim. And no room at all.
Wh-where do I go? On the roof?!
My numbers say four of us fit. Not five.
Then we pack lighter. Lose the grape!
Out goes the grape. And a napkin. And some of Bup's pride.
The lid still won't close. It isn't even close.
So one of us rides in the truck. In a sock.
N-no! The truck is dark! Boxes fall in trucks!
If this lid won't shut by morning, someone stays behind.
Upstairs, a door creaks. Slow footsteps. Someone wants a snack.
Four bros dive into the lunchbox. Pim dives under it.
It's Dad. In socks. He opens the pantry and yawns.
He grabs crackers. He stares right at the lunchbox.
Don't see me. I'm a strawberry. A tiny strawberry.
Dad shrugs, munches a cracker, and shuffles back upstairs.
Pim? You can come out now. It's safe.
Zeek, there's a little door down here. Under the box.
A door? Lunchboxes don't have doors. That's absurd.
Pim pushes. A flat drawer slides out of the bottom.
It's a two-floor lunchbox. Zeek only measured the top floor.
I measured from above. I never once looked underneath.
I always look underneath. That's where I hide.
Nice work, little bean. Seriously. Nice work.
But the drawer is packed. Forty crayons. Mia's whole rainbow.
If we dump them, Mia loses her colors. No way.
Then we carry them. To her pencil case. All of them.
Five Dough Bros carry crayons like logs. Trip after trip.
Pim drops the blue one. It rolls under the shelf.
N-not the blue! Blue is her favorite! Everybody knows that!
Crispy glows under the shelf like a flashlight. Pim grabs it.
Bup and Lolly up top. Zeek, Pim and Crispy downstairs.
It's cozy. Nobody touch my ember.
I f-found a door. Me. I'm a finder now.
New rule. Before I measure anything, I ask Pim.
They fall asleep on two floors, snoring in perfect stereo.
Dawn. Car doors slam. Mia grabs the lunchbox and runs outside.
Dad takes it. 'One second, sweetie.' It goes on the car roof.
He climbs in. The engine starts. Dad never checks the roof.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
